title: FA/234/2022 of MANOJ RAWAT Vs HIMANI DEVI

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Hon'ble Smt. Justice Ritu Bahri, CJ.
And
Hon'ble Sri Justice Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
First Appeal No. 234 of 2022

Manoj Rawat. ..............Appellant.
Versus
Smt. Himani Devi. ............Respondents
Present:
Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, learned Counsel for the appellant.
JUDGMENT : (per Hon'ble Mr. Justice Rakesh Thapliyal)
1. The instant first appeal has been preferred by the appellant
against the judgment and order dated 13.10.2022 passed by Judge
Family Court, Tehri Garhwal in Original Suit No. 01 of 2021
(Manoj Rawat Vs. Himani Rawat) whereby petition filed by the
present appellant under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act,
1955 for seeking divorce has been dismissed.
2. There is a delay of 33 days' in filing the instant appeal.
Consequently, on 16.05.2023 notices were issued to the
respondent in the delay condonation application as well as in the
appeal. Office report dated 03.08.2023 indicates that notices were
served to the respondent personally but despite personal service
no one put appearance on behalf of respondent. In the interest of
justice, again fresh notices were issued to the respondent on
12.03.2024 and in addition to normal mode of service, appellant
was permitted to serve the respondent through Dasti. In
compliance thereto, steps were taken by the appellant to serve
notice to respondent and on 10.04.2024, appellant filed an
affidavit of service and office report dated 29.05.2024 indicates

2
that notice upon respondent is served personally. Since the
service is complete but no one put appearance on her behalf
consequently, this Court has no option except to decide the
present appeal on its own merits.
3. Delay is explained satisfactorily, therefore, delay
condonation application no. 01 of 2022 is allowed.
4. The brief facts of the case are that appellant married with
the respondent on 10.06.2019 and after marriage, they lived
together almost for a period of 2-3 months and during this period
behaviour of respondent towards plaintiff appellant and his
family was normal and thereafter, she frequently used to visit her
parents' home and in the month of October, 2019 when the
opposite party - respondent wife was pregnant, then she
informed the appellant that she does not want to continue this
pregnancy and she insisted to visit her parental home.
Subsequently, respondent wife telephonically informed to the
appellant that she has taken medicine of abortion and then,
present appellant got annoyed and since then between both of
them differences arose and after some time, she left the
matrimonial home and thereafter, she never came back. Many
attempts were made by the appellant to bring her back but she
always refused. Thereafter, on 01.02.2021, appellant filed a suit
for seeking divorce on the ground of cruelty under Section 13 of
the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 wherein he prayed for grant of
decree of divorce and dissolution of marriage.
5. While deciding the suit, the Judge, Family Court, framed
two issues on 11.05.2022, which are as follows:
"(i) Whether opposite party has committed any cruel
behaviour with the plaintiff after solemnization of marriage? If
yes, then its effects.

3
(ii) Whether plaintiff is entitled for the relief prayed for in the
plaint?"
6. Both the issues were decided against the plaintiff -
appellant and the Judge, Family Court, Tehri Garhwal, dismissed
the suit filed by the plaintiff under Section 13 of the Hindu
Marriage Act on 13.10.2022, which is being assailed by the
appellant in the instant first appeal.
7. Admittedly, the marriage was solemnized between the
parties on 10.06.2019 and thereafter, both of them are living
separately since October, 2019 and there is no issue from this
marriage.
8. Though both the issues were decided against the appellant
and the suit filed by the appellant seeking divorce on the ground
of cruelty was dismissed but admittedly, since October, 2019,
both the parties are living separately and there is no issue and
therefore, it appears to be a dead marriage.
9. Learned counsel for the appellant has placed reliance on the
judgments rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court on the issue
of dead marriage i.e. in the case of Samar Ghosh Vs. Jaya
Ghosh2007 (4) SCC 511, Shilpa Sailesh Vs. Varun Sreenivasan
2023 SCC Online SC 544 and Prakash Chandra Joshi Vs. Kuntal
Prakash Chandra Joshi @ Kuntal Visanji Shah 2024 INSC 55.
10. We have perused all the judgments relied upon by the
learned counsel for the appellant and keeping in view the fact
that both the parties in the present appeal are living separately
since October, 2019, therefore, we are of the view that this Court
should grant divorce to the parties, who are living separately
since 2019, as separation also amounts to mental cruelty. In such
view of the matter, present appeal deserves to be allowed.

4
Accordingly, First appeal is allowed. Judgment and order dated
13.10.2022 passed by the Judge, Family Court, Tehri Garhwal in
O.S. No. 01 of 2021 (Manoj Rawat Vs. Himani Rawat) is set aside.
Marriage between the parties dated 10.06.2019 is dissolved by
passing decree of divorce.
11. Apart from this, respondent wife, as per information as
given by the learned counsel for the appellant, is living in Tehri
Garhwal and both of them are living separately since October,
2019 and there is no issue from this marriage, this Court is of the
view that the appellant should pay an amount of Rs. 5,00,000/-
to the respondent wife towards permanent alimony, which the
appellant shall deposit before District Legal Service Authority,
Tehri Garhwal, within two months from today and the District
Legal Service Authority will contact with the respondent wife
and give her this amount.
 _____________
 Ritu Bahri, CJ.
